lessons.title: Container Glass: Bottles and Jars
lessons.body:
Container glass is the most common glass product in Africa, used for beverages, food, medicine, and cosmetics. In Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya, and Egypt, bottle-making plants produce millions of units daily. The process starts with a batch mix of silica sand (about 60%), soda ash (20%), limestone (15%), and recycled glass (cullet) (5-40%). Cullet saves energy and raw materials. The mix is melted in a furnace at 1500-1600Â°C. Molten glass is cut into gobs and fed into a forming machine. Two methods dominate: blow-and-blow for narrow-neck bottles (beer, soda) and press-and-blow for wide-mouth jars (jam, mayonnaise).

A critical step is annealing: the hot bottles pass through a lehr (a long oven) that gradually cools them from about 550Â°C to room temperature over 30-60 minutes. Without annealing, bottles crack easily. After cooling, they are inspected for defects like stones (unmelted sand), bubbles, and cracks. Automated machines use cameras and lasers, but manual inspection on a lighted table is still common in small plants.

In Africa, recycling is a big part of container glass. Collectors bring used bottles to depots, where they are sorted by colour (clear, green, brown). Mixed colours lower the quality of new glass. A simple test: hold two bottles togetherâif the colour looks different, keep them separate. Bottles are washed, crushed into cullet (2-5 cm pieces), and fed back into the furnace. This reduces melting energy by 25-30% compared to using all raw materials.

Starting a small container glass workshop is capital-intensive, but repair and decoration are accessible. You can etch, paint, or sandblast bottles for sale as decorative items. For a basic bottle-cutting jig, you need a glass cutter, a candle, and cold water. Score the bottle, heat the score line, then dip in waterâit snaps cleanly. Safety: always wear leather gloves and safety glasses. Container glass is 100% recyclable infinitely, making it a sustainable business.

lessons.title: Flat Glass: Windows and Automotive
lessons.body:
Flat glass is used for windows, doors, mirrors, and vehicle glazing. It is made by floating molten glass on a bath of molten tinâthe float process. The glass spreads evenly, producing a smooth, parallel surface. In Africa, major float lines exist in Egypt, South Africa, and Nigeria. For a small-scale processor, you buy large sheets (jumbo sizes like 3.21m x 2.25m) and cut them to size.

Cutting flat glass requires a clean surface, a straight edge, and a glass cutter with a carbide wheel. Score one firm line from edge to edgeâdo not go back over it. Then tap gently under the score with the ball end of the cutter, and the glass will crack along the line. For thick glass (6mm+), use a running pliers. Always wear safety glasses and gloves. Edges are sharp; you must seam them with a diamond pad or fine sandpaper to prevent cuts.

For windows, the most common types are clear float (3-6mm), tinted (bronze, grey, green), and low-emissivity (low-E) for heat control. In hot African climates, tinted or reflective glass reduces solar heat gain by up to 60%. Laminated glass (two layers with a plastic interlayer) is used for car windshields and security windows. It holds together when broken. Tempered glass is 4-5 times stronger than annealed glass and breaks into small, blunt piecesâused for car side windows and shower doors.

Automotive glass includes windshields (laminated) and side/rear windows (tempered). Replacing a windshield requires urethane adhesive, primers, and a caulking gun. The old glass is cut out with a cold knife or wire. The frame is cleaned, primed, and new urethane applied. The windshield is set, and the car must sit for 1 hour before driving (24 hours for full cure). In many African cities, mobile glass fitters do this on the roadside. Tools: suction cup lifters, glass cleaner, and a torque wrench for setting. Safety: never use a screwdriver to pry glassâit can shatter. Use proper auto glass tools.

lessons.title: Fiberglass and Insulation
lessons.body:
Fiberglass is made by forcing molten glass through tiny holes to create thin fibers, then coating them with a binder. It is used for insulation, boat hulls, car bodies, and water tanks. In Africa, fiberglass insulation is common in roofs and walls to reduce heat. The fibers trap air, slowing heat transfer. A typical fiberglass batt has an R-value of 2.5 to 3.5 per inch. For a hot roof, 100mm of fiberglass insulation can lower indoor temperature by 5-10Â°C.

Making fiberglass at small scale is possible but dangerous. You need a furnace at 1200Â°C, a bushing (a platinum-rhodium plate with hundreds of holes), and a high-speed winder. The fibers are pulled at 1000-3000 m/min, then sprayed with resin and chopped into strands. For a safer start, buy raw fiberglass mat or chopped strand and use it for lay-up. Boat building and water tank repair are common businesses. You need polyester resin, catalyst (MEKP), and fiberglass cloth. Mix resin with 1-2% catalyst, apply to cloth, and roll out bubbles. Cure time is 20-30 minutes. Always work in a ventilated area and wear a respiratorâfiberglass dust irritates lungs.

Insulation installation is less risky. For a typical African home, you can install fiberglass batts in the ceiling. Wear gloves, long sleeves, and a dust mask. Cut batts with a utility knife, leaving a 2cm gap around wires. Do not compress the insulationâit loses R-value. For pipes, use fiberglass pipe wrap. In Nigeria, fiberglass water tanks are made by hand lay-up on a mold. The mold is waxed, gel coat sprayed, then layers of resin and mat applied. After curing, the tank is popped out and fitted with a lid and outlet. This business needs a workshop, resin, and a moldâstart-up cost around $2,000.

Safety note: fiberglass fibers can embed in skin. Wash with cold water and mild soapânever rub. Always wear protective clothing.

lessons.title: Optical Glass and Lenses
lessons.body:
Optical glass is high-purity glass with precise refractive index and low distortion. It is used for eyeglasses, cameras, microscopes, and binoculars. In Africa, the demand for eyeglasses is hugeâover 100 million people need vision correction. Making optical glass from scratch requires a furnace with platinum crucibles and strict temperature control, which is beyond most small workshops. But lens grinding and fitting is a viable business.

To make a simple lens, you start with a glass blank (a thick disc). You grind the curve using a cast-iron tool and abrasive grits: first 80-grit silicon carbide, then 220, 400, 600, and finally 1200 for fine grinding. Each stage takes 10-30 minutes of hand or machine grinding. The curve is checked with a spherometer. After grinding, you polish with cerium oxide slurry on a felt pad. Polishing takes 30-60 minutes until the lens is clear. Then you edge the lens to fit a frame using a diamond wheel.

For eyeglasses, you need a lensometer to measure prescription, a edger, and a frame heater. A basic set costs $1,500-$3,000. In many African countries, opticians import semi-finished blanks and grind the prescription curve on the back surface. That is faster and cheaper. You can also make simple magnifying lenses by grinding a convex curve on a glass disc. For a 2x magnifier, the focal length is 125mm. Use the formula: power (diopters) = 1000 / focal length (mm). So 8 diopters = 125mm.

Safety: glass dust from grinding is harmfulâwear a respirator and goggles. Keep grits wet to prevent dust. Clean all tools between grits to avoid scratches. Optical work requires patience and precision. In Africa, mobile opticians travel to rural areas with a trial lens set and a simple grinder. They cut and fit lenses on-site. That is a low-cost entry point: a trial set, a hand edger, and a frame warmer. You can start for under $500.

lessons.title: Laboratory Glassware
lessons.body:
Laboratory glassware must resist heat, chemicals, and thermal shock. Borosilicate glass (like Pyrex) is the standard because it has a low expansion coefficient (3.3 x 10^-6 /Â°C). Soda-lime glass cracks when heated. In Africa, university and school labs, medical clinics, and research centres need beakers, flasks, test tubes, pipettes, and petri dishes. Most are imported, but you can repair, clean, and even make simple items.

To make a test tube from borosilicate tubing, you need a bench torch (propane-oxygen) that reaches 1200Â°C. Cut the tubing to length with a triangular file, then rotate in the flame until the ends soften. Round the ends by blowing gently. For a beaker, you need a larger tube, a flat bottom (sealed by heating and pressing), and a spout (formed by pulling with a carbon rod). Anneal in a kiln at 560Â°C for 30 minutes, then cool slowly. Without annealing, the glass will crack.

Cleaning lab glassware is a common service. Use a chromic acid solution (dangerousâwear acid gloves and goggles) or a laboratory detergent. For stubborn stains, soak in 10% nitric acid. Rinse with distilled water. Never use abrasive padsâthey scratch and harbor bacteria. For volumetric flasks and pipettes, calibration matters. You can check a 100ml flask by weighing the water it holds: 100ml of water at 20Â°C weighs 99.82g. If it is off by more than 0.1g, it is not accurate for analysis.

Repairing broken glassware is possible for simple breaks. A broken beaker rim can be fire-polished. A cracked flask cannot be repairedâdiscard it. For a small lab business, focus on cleaning, calibration, and making simple items like stirring rods, spatulas, and drying racks. You can also make custom glass apparatus for local schoolsâlike a simple distillation head. Start-up: a torch, tubing, a small kiln, and safety gearâabout $1,000. Safety: always wear a face shield and heat-resistant gloves. Never heat a closed container.

lessons.title: Artistic and Decorative Glass
lessons.body:
Artistic glass uses colour, texture, and shape to create beauty. In Africa, traditional glass beads, stained glass windows, and fused glass are popular. The raw material is often recycled bottle glass, which is cheap and available. You can make beads, pendants, plates, and window hangings.

To make a glass bead, you need a torch (propane or MAPP gas), mandrels (steel rods), and glass rods (COE 104 for soft glass). Heat the rod in the flame until it glows orange, then wrap the molten glass around a mandrel that has been coated with bead release. Build the bead, add colour with stringers or frit, then shape with a graphite paddle. Anneal the beads in a kiln at 510Â°C for 30 minutes, then cool slowly. A single bead takes 2-5 minutes to make. A kilo of glass rods costs $20-$30 and makes about 200 beads. Sell beads for $0.50-$2 each.

Fused glass is another technique. You cut flat glass (2-6mm) into shapes, stack them, and fire in a kiln to 800Â°C. The glass melts and fuses together. For a slump (to make a bowl), you fire to 620Â°C over a mold. You need a kiln with a controllerâcost $500-$1,500. Glass powders (frit) and stringers add colour. Always use compatible glass (same COE) to avoid cracks. In South Africa and Kenya, fused glass jewellery and coasters sell well at craft markets.

Stained glass uses lead came or copper foil to join coloured glass pieces. You need a glass cutter, grozing pliers, a soldering iron, and lead came. Cut each piece, grind edges, then assemble. Solder the joints. A small panel (30cm x 30cm) takes 4-6 hours. Safety: lead is toxicâwear a respirator when soldering and wash hands. For a low-cost start, try bottle glass slumping: flatten bottles in a kiln and shape into cheese boards or spoon rests. One kiln load (10 bottles) takes 8 hours and sells for $50-$100. This is a profitable craft business in many African cities.

quiz.q: What is the main advantage of adding cullet (recycled glass) to a container glass batch?
options: A) It reduces melting energy by 25-30%
B) It makes the glass stronger
C) It changes the colour to green
D) It eliminates the need for annealing
quiz.explanation: Cullet lowers the melting temperature, saving energy and raw materials.

quiz.q: Which forming method is used for narrow-neck bottles like beer bottles?
quiz.explanation: Blow-and-blow is standard for narrow-neck containers because it shapes the neck first.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of annealing container glass?
options: B) To strengthen the glass by cooling it slowly
C) To make the glass lighter
quiz.explanation: Annealing relieves internal stresses, preventing cracks.

quiz.q: Which colour of bottle glass is most difficult to recycle into clear glass?
quiz.explanation: Green glass contains iron and chromium, which contaminate clear glass.

quiz.q: What simple tool can help you cut a bottle cleanly at home?
options: B) A glass cutter and candle
quiz.explanation: Scoring with a glass cutter and applying heat then cold water causes a clean break.

quiz.q: What is the float process used for?
quiz.explanation: Float glass is made by floating molten glass on molten tin to create flat, smooth sheets.

quiz.q: Which type of glass is used for car windshields?
quiz.explanation: Laminated glass has a plastic interlayer that holds fragments together on impact.

quiz.q: What is the correct way to cut a sheet of flat glass?
options: A) Score one firm line and tap under it
D) Heat it with a torch
quiz.explanation: A single score line followed by tapping underneath produces a clean break.

quiz.q: What is the R-value of typical fiberglass insulation per inch?
quiz.explanation: Fiberglass batts have an R-value of about 2.5 to 3.5 per inch of thickness.

quiz.q: What catalyst is commonly used with polyester resin in fiberglass lay-up?
quiz.explanation: MEKP (methyl ethyl ketone peroxide) initiates curing of polyester resin.

quiz.q: Why should you never compress fiberglass insulation?
quiz.explanation: Compressing reduces the air pockets that provide insulation.

quiz.q: What safety gear is essential when handling fiberglass?
quiz.explanation: Fiberglass dust irritates lungs and skin, so a respirator and gloves are needed.

quiz.q: What type of glass is used for most laboratory glassware?
quiz.explanation: Borosilicate glass resists thermal shock and chemical attack.

quiz.q: What is the annealing temperature for borosilicate glass?
quiz.explanation: Borosilicate glass is annealed at about 560Â°C to relieve stress.

quiz.q: How can you check the accuracy of a 100ml volumetric flask?
options: A) Weigh the water it holds
quiz.explanation: 100ml of water at 20Â°C weighs 99.82g; deviation indicates inaccuracy.

quiz.q: What is the COE for soft glass used in bead making?
quiz.explanation: Soft glass rods for bead making typically have a COE of 104.

quiz.q: What temperature is used to fuse glass in a kiln?
quiz.explanation: Full fuse occurs around 800Â°C; slumping is lower at about 620Â°C.

quiz.q: What is a mandrel used for in glass bead making?
options: B) To hold the bead while forming
quiz.explanation: The mandrel is a steel rod that the molten glass is wrapped around, forming the hole.

quiz.q: What safety precaution is critical when soldering stained glass?
options: B) Work in a dark room
quiz.explanation: Lead solder fumes are toxic; a respirator prevents inhalation.

quiz.q: What is a low-cost way to start an artistic glass business?
options: B) Slump recycled bottles in a kiln
quiz.explanation: Bottle slumping requires only a small kiln and recycled bottles.

quiz.q: Which of these is NOT a common container glass product?
quiz.explanation: Window pane is flat glass, not container glass.

quiz.q: What is the approximate melting temperature of container glass batch?
quiz.explanation: Container glass melts at 1500-1600Â°C in a furnace.

quiz.q: Which type of flat glass reduces solar heat gain by up to 60%?
quiz.explanation: Tinted or reflective glass reflects solar radiation, reducing heat.

quiz.q: What is the main risk of using a screwdriver to remove a car windshield?
options: B) It can shatter the glass
quiz.explanation: Screwdrivers can crack or shatter the windshield; proper auto glass tools are needed.

quiz.q: What is the function of a gel coat in fiberglass water tank production?
options: A) To provide a smooth, protective surface
quiz.explanation: Gel coat is the outer resin layer that gives a smooth finish and protects against water.

quiz.q: What is the typical cure time for polyester resin with MEKP catalyst?
quiz.explanation: With 1-2% MEKP, polyester resin cures in 20-30 minutes at room temperature.

quiz.q: What is the formula to calculate lens power in diopters?
quiz.explanation: Diopters = 1000 divided by focal length in millimetres.

quiz.q: Which abrasive grit is used for the final fine grinding of a lens?
quiz.explanation: 1200-grit is the finest grinding stage before polishing.

quiz.q: What is the purpose of a spherometer in lens making?
options: A) To measure the curve of the lens
quiz.explanation: A spherometer measures the radius of curvature of the ground surface.

quiz.q: Why is borosilicate glass preferred for labware over soda-lime glass?
options: C) It is easier to melt
quiz.explanation: Borosilicate has a low expansion coefficient, so it doesn't crack when heated.
